sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 1 'Alphabet' (pp. 589-590) lists vowels a e i o u, diphthongs, consonants w r k t n m p h f s, says vowels have long and short sounds (doubling marks length), describes the glottal 'break', notes r less rolled than Sa'a and 'no closed syllables'; no word on accent/stress anywhere in the article (a full-text search for stress/accent two independent OCRs for accent/stress/penult/syllable: none).

sources.citation: Flavelle, Darren. 2017 [publ. 2018]. Reduplication in Oroha: The multifaceted process and its effects within the language's grammar. In Le, Uy-Di Nancy (ed.), Proceedings 2017: Selected papers from the 21st College-wide Conference for Students in Languages, Linguistics & Literature, 18-24. Honolulu: NFLRC (RN55). hdl 10125/58832.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2 'Phoneme inventory' gives only the segment table (p t k m n r[ɾ] s h w ʔ; a e i o u); footnote 9 remarks coda consonants are generally disallowed. No stress/accent statement. Mentions an unpublished sketch grammar and 'The Oroha Lexicon' (Lachler & Wells-Jensen).

sources.citation: Wells-Jensen, Sheri; Wells-Jensen, Jason; Fullenkamp, Lucas. 2015. Involving students in meaningful language preservation work as early as possible. ICLDC 4 presentation (slides), ScholarSpace hdl 10125/25292.
sources.note: Nothing; describes the BGSU Oroha dictionary/elicitation project (Skype sessions with Oroha consultants), no linguistic description.

sources.citation: Lynch, John, Malcolm Ross & Terry Crowley. 2002. The Oceanic Languages. Richmond: Curzon.
sources.note: Oroha appears only in subgrouping lists ('Are'are-Oroha-Marau) and the language listing (p. 885); no sketch, no stress information for Oroha.

sources.citation: Lachler, Jordan & Sheri Wells-Jensen (with research assistants incl. D. Flavelle). n.d. [c. 2012-2017]. Oroha sketch grammar and 'The Oroha Lexicon' / Oroha-English dictionary (Bowling Green State University / University of Alberta Oroha dictionary project). Unpublished; possibly a Webonary site.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only modern first-hand description of Oroha (cited by Flavelle 2017 as 'Lachler and Jensen, unpublished' sketch grammar); a phonology chapter would be the natural place for a stress statement. Ask the authors (swellsj@bgsu.edu per the 2015 slides) or check webonary.org/oroha and scholarworks.bgsu.edu, both could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Flavelle, Darren. 2015. Field Notes on Oroha. Unpublished (cited in Flavelle 2017); any later Flavelle thesis on Oroha (University of Alberta / UH Manoa) if one exists.
